_comment: Input for gen_regions.py. Each entry becomes one neighborhood polygon in data/japan.geojson. center is [lat, lng]; radius_m is the rough walkable extent used to generate a natural-looking boundary (these are illustrative areas, not surveyed/administrative boundaries). blurb = one-line, always visible on the map. notes = deeper description, shown only in the click popup. Re-run the script after editing this file.

regions.name: Shibuya
regions.blurb: The scramble crossing, vertical malls, and youth fashion.
regions.notes: Center Gai for arcades and cheap food, Dogenzaka for nightlife up the hill, Miyashita Park's rooftop, and Shibuya Sky for the observation deck view back down at the crossing.

regions.name: Shinjuku East / Kabukicho
regions.blurb: Neon nightlife blocks, Golden Gai, and Omoide Yokocho.
regions.notes: Kabukicho is the entertainment district proper (bars, karaoke, the Godzilla head on the Toho building); Golden Gai's ~200 tiny bars sit just southeast; Omoide Yokocho's yakitori alleys are right by the station's west exit. Isetan and Shinjuku Gyoen are an easy walk south.

regions.name: Harajuku / Omotesando
regions.blurb: Teen fashion alley next to a tree-lined design boulevard.
regions.notes: Takeshita-dori is the crowded, colorful youth-fashion street; Omotesando is the wide, quiet, tree-lined avenue of flagship stores just south of it. Meiji Shrine's forest entrance is at the west end.

regions.name: Shimokitazawa
regions.blurb: Vintage shops, tiny live-music bars, low-rise and walkable.
regions.notes: A maze of narrow car-free lanes around the station with secondhand clothing, indie theaters, and small live houses. Quieter and more local than the big-name districts; good for an afternoon wander.

regions.name: Asakusa
regions.blurb: Senso-ji, Nakamise market street, old-Tokyo riverside feel.
regions.notes: Nakamise-dori runs straight from the Kaminarimon gate to Senso-ji, lined with souvenir and snack stalls. The Sumida riverfront and Tokyo Skytree view are a short walk east across the river.

regions.name: Akihabara
regions.blurb: Electronics, anime/manga stores, arcades, maid cafes.
regions.notes: Multi-floor electronics and hobby stores line the main strip north from the station; side streets have retro-game shops, arcades, and idol/maid cafes. Gets loud and crowded on weekends.

regions.name: Ginza
regions.blurb: Upscale flagship shopping and old-money department stores.
regions.notes: Chuo-dori closes to cars on weekend afternoons, turning the main strip into a pedestrian shopping street. Kabuki-za theater is at the southeast edge if you want a short-act ticket.

regions.name: Roppongi
regions.blurb: Nightlife strip by day, major art museums by daylight.
regions.notes: Roppongi Hills and Tokyo Midtown anchor the art-museum side (Mori Art Museum, National Art Center nearby); after dark the streets toward Roppongi Crossing turn into one of Tokyo's busiest bar/club areas, popular with tourists and expats.

regions.name: Ueno
regions.blurb: Big park with museums and a zoo, plus a chaotic market street.
regions.notes: Ueno Park holds the Tokyo National Museum, the zoo, and a famous cherry-blossom tunnel in spring. Ameyoko, the old black-market street, runs along the train tracks just south with cheap food and stalls.

regions.name: Nakameguro
regions.blurb: Canal-side cafes and boutiques, famous for spring blossoms.
regions.notes: The Meguro River is lined with cherry trees (packed at peak bloom, lit up at night) and, year-round, small independent cafes, bakeries, and clothing shops. Quieter and more residential than the big districts.
